claim_boundary: Static blind-journey execution consumer: executor success defines that one scripted journey deterministically produces one stamped, validator-accepted blind-journey receipt; it claims no installed usefulness, no candidate qualification, no blind acceptance and no release verdict.
limitations: scripted executor success cannot qualify a candidate; the real candidate-bound run waits on the accepted #4510 harness and the frozen #1609 candidate
per-kind digest presence binds this executor consumer only; the RIPR-SPEC-0200 contract corpus stays digest-optional at its own schema version

declared observations bind to the recorded canonical execution outputs (`exit:<n>`, `static:<movement>`, `receipt:<state>`) of the last execution of each kind; the contract corpus keeps declaration-only axis evidence at its own schema version
candidate/process/artifact admission is referenced, not owned; #4510 stays the admission authority
operator classes and the human/agent first-hour observation recorded on #4604 are planning inputs for the real run, not outputs of this offline executor
the ten installed-Rust scripted rows bind the retained RIPR-SPEC-0207 fixture snapshots, not a live package or process identity
the eleven installed-Python scripted rows bind the retained RIPR-SPEC-0209 fixture snapshots, not a live interpreter, pytest or package identity
combinations_not_exercised: a real installed candidate execution through the #4510 harness (#4604)
a real operator or model session against public docs and help (#4508, #4516/#4518/#4519)
a terminal result of instrument_failure, which requires a broken or absent packet rather than an executable script
a real process-interrupt receipt journey, which still needs the process-admission surface (#4510) even though the scripted interruption recovery is now exercised
